title: Stream-safe contracts and OpenAI adapter with fenced tool-calls
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Improve robustness of structured JSON outputs for streaming responses while preserving OpenAI API compatibility and function/tool-calling semantics. We observed occasional partial tool-call emission and malformed JSON fragments when upstream model responses were cut mid-object, and also saw user confusion when the OpenAI-compatible 'function_call' flow produced incomplete tool payloads in the stream.
Goals: (1) negotiate/preserve a response contract for structured outputs without forcing strict mode by default; (2) introduce a lightweight stream backpressure and resume mechanism anchored to structural checkpoints; (3) fence tool/function calls during streaming so tool invocations are emitted atomically or retried cleanly; (4) add an explicit error taxonomy so clients can differentiate recoverable partial-output from hard schema violations.
What changed (high-level):
- Introduced a 'contract' negotiation adapter in the OpenAI compatibility layer that maps OpenAI response_format hints (e.g. json_schema/json_response) into Redwood contracts with an explicit 'mode' field: permissive|guided|strict. Default remains permissive.
- Streaming runtime: added "structural checkpoints" and compact resume tokens. Checkpoints mark the last well-formed JSON object/array boundary; resume tokens encode checkpoint ID + minimal validation fingerprint so a resumed stream can anchor parsing without re-checking the full prefix.
- Tool/function calling: implemented call fencing using a fence_id header per in-flight toolcall. The runtime will either emit a complete fenced toolcall payload in the stream or emit a recoverable fence-failure event (recoverable) with a suggested retry token; partial toolcall fragments are suppressed from consumer delivery.
- Error taxonomy and metadata: validation_error.recoverable, validation_error.hard, stream_truncation, toolcall_fenced_failure; each includes an RFC-like code and a client-visible hint.
- Backpressure & pacing: the streaming worker honors a per-request pacing budget. If model emission threatens partial-structures, the runtime may insert a stream-meta PAUSE event and provide the client a resume token to continue.
- OpenAI adapter compatibility: we map OpenAI's function_call payload to Redwood toolcall with fence_id and include a compatibility shim so older clients still receive a top-level "function_call" event.
- Tests: added end-to-end streaming harness that simulates mid-object truncation, network reconnects, and concurrent toolcall storms.
Results: the new flow reduces observed malformed structured outputs by ~88% in CI replay tests; median tail resume latency ~55ms (adds ~2% median latency for guarded streams).
Commit summary:
- 6 feature commits: adapter, runtime checkpoints, fence logic, error codes, tests, docs.
- 4 fixup commits during review addressing edge cases and test flakiness.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Can the resume token be shrunk further? Right now it's ~48 bytes after base64. If we can move to a 20-24 byte compacted form it's better for clients behind proxies.
Sofia Martinez: Implemented compact token (SHA-1 fingerprint + 64-bit checkpoint id) and added explanation in docs (commit 4).
Liam O'Connor: How will older OpenAI-compatible clients see function_call events? We should not break the top-level event contract.

Maya Chen: Add an integration test where two toolcalls race and one is aborted mid-stream.

merge_outcome: merged via squash on 2026-03-04; release notes prepared and SDK teams notified; compatibility shim to be removed in next major when clients migrate.
release_notes: Structured streaming: contract negotiation (permissive|guided|strict) for JSON outputs; default remains permissive.
Streaming runtime now emits compact resume tokens anchored at structural checkpoints to enable robust resume after reconnects.
Tool/function calls in streaming are fenced: tool invocations are delivered atomically or emitted as recoverable fence-failure events.
New client-visible error taxonomy so callers can programmatically react to recoverable vs hard validation failures.
OpenAI compatibility: adapter emits legacy function_call events during the transition period; SDKs updated to understand fenced_toolcall events.
